name: Followers of Morrigan

abilities.name: Shield Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close formation and raises shields.

abilities.name: Frenzy
abilities.text: Improves a unit's attack capabilities for an extended period of time.

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

attributes.name: Berserk
attributes.text: This unit can go berserk during the battle. This makes them uncontrollable, they will automatically attack nearby enemies.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Guerrilla Deployment
attributes.text: This unit can deploy outside of the deployment zone.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Raider
attributes.text: This unit may set buildings on fire, cause more fire damage with torches and capture faster than other units.

attributes.name: Scare (everyone)
attributes.text: This unit frightens all enemy units.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Freedom, glory and the chaos of battle. What else is there?
history: The Morrigan – the great, shape-shifting phantom queen of Celtic mythology – was the patron goddess of many things; variously death, war, revenge, fate, magic, prophecy, horses and the night all fell under her sphere of influence. She was said to have taken the form of the raven to fly over the battlefield, leading an army of undead soldiers, influencing the direction of the fight and deciding its outcome. The Morrigan had two other aspects, Nemain and Badb, who presided over the fury and venom of the combat respectively. Once the battle was over and the survivors had left the field, the Morrigan claimed her “acorn crop” – the heads of the slain as her trophies. Warriors aspired to bravery and heroism to gain the goddess’ favour and secure victory.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
